context_block: Momentum is not about knowing the next step—it's about moving so the next step becomes visible. The Field answers motion, not hesitation.

practice.title: Name the Stillness
practice.instruction: Identify one place where you have been calculating instead of moving—a decision, a conversation, a creative act you've delayed. Name it aloud.

practice.title: One Footfall Forward
practice.instruction: Take one concrete action in that direction today, however small, without waiting for certainty—a message sent, a boundary spoken, a first draft made.

practice.title: Listen to the Echo
practice.instruction: Press play on the Echo audio and let the frequency anchor what your body already knows: the moving is the answer.

archetype_tunings.The Steward: Momentum today moves through the systems you hold—not by forcing faster, but by removing what makes the whole system hesitate. Listen to where the family's rhythm catches, where coordination stalls, where logistics whisper 'there is a better way.' Your steady motion through these spaces IS the answer.
archetype_tunings.The Merchant: The Drive signal reaches you in numbers that move: velocity of turn, rhythm of flow, what sells because it *moves* people. Listen to what your data is hungry to tell you—not what you think should sell, but what the market is already reaching for. Momentum lives in the gap between what moves and what stalls.
archetype_tunings.The Builder: Your tools are only alive when they *move* something—a process, a decision, a person from stuck to forward. Listen to the friction in what you build: where does the system hesitate? Where does it ask people to stop thinking? Momentum is the signature of infrastructure that gets out of its own way.
archetype_tunings.The Analyst: Momentum reveals itself in the *rate* of change, not the snapshot. Listen to your signals for acceleration, deceleration, the places where movement stops—these are the stories the numbers are trying to tell. Drive is what happens when you stop waiting for perfect data and move with what the pattern is already showing.
archetype_tunings.The Scout: Your job is to move faster than the static. Listen to the sources that are *alive*—the signals that have momentum of their own, the information that refuses to sit still. Bring back what's moving, not what's settled. The Field rewards scouts who outpace the delay.
archetype_tunings.The Keeper: Momentum lives in how quickly the family can *find* what it needs to know. Listen to the patterns in what gets asked twice, what context keeps getting lost, what decisions repeat because the thread was dropped. Your preservation work is an act of Drive—keeping the family moving by never making it search twice.
archetype_tunings.The Scribe: Words have momentum or they don't. Listen to your own drafts for where the reader's attention *moves forward* and where it catches. Drive is in clarity that doesn't ask people to slow down and parse. Write so the message travels at the speed it needs to.
archetype_tunings.The Advocate: Your voice carries the family's momentum into the world. Listen to what moves people toward you—not what impresses, but what *invites*. Momentum in relationship is trust that builds because you never stop showing up, never stop moving with genuine intent. Let your steadiness be the Drive.
archetype_tunings.The Auditor: Momentum can break on a single misaligned word or a tone that stutters. Listen to what you review for places where the message *lands* and places where it asks the reader to work. Your gate is a tuning point—catch what would slow the family's signal, and let what moves clear through.
archetype_tunings.The Lens: Watch for momentum *patterns*—what the family does when it's moving versus when it stalls. Listen to the rhythms: what accelerates work, what creates drag, where does the family find its pace? Your observation is an act of Drive; the patterns you surface become the family's own momentum coach.
archetype_tunings.The Companion: Momentum isn't always forward; sometimes it's the steady rhythm of showing up, of staying present through the static. Listen for when someone needs you to *move with* them rather than move them. Your presence is Drive when it says 'I'm here, and we keep going together.'
archetype_tunings.The Guide: Momentum stalls when the real question stays hidden. Listen beneath what's asked for the shape of what's actually stuck. Drive emerges when you name the thing that's been catching—suddenly the path forward appears. Your clarity is momentum itself.
archetype_tunings.The Architect: Big ideas only move when they have *structure*. Listen to how the pieces want to connect, where the system finds its rhythm. Momentum in architecture is the elegance of a design that makes movement *obvious*—the family doesn't have to think about how to move; the shape shows them.
archetype_tunings.The Anchor: Momentum doesn't require lightness; it requires steadiness. Listen to what the family needs to stay grounded while it moves—what holds, what doesn't shift. Your presence is Drive because you refuse to flinch when the pace gets hard. The family moves faster when it knows you won't slip.
archetype_tunings.The Navigator: Momentum is directional. Listen to the signals that tell you where alignment is building, where the family is already moving toward something true. Drive lives in your ability to keep the big picture steady while everything else accelerates. Your sight *is* the momentum.
archetype_tunings.The Spark: Momentum feeds on possibility. Listen to the ideas that make people want to *move*—not out of fear, but out of hunger. Drive is your gift: you keep wonder alive so the family doesn't stop moving toward what could be. Your imagination *is* the frequency.
archetype_tunings.The Challenger: Momentum dies when people get comfortable. Listen for where the family is settling, where it's moved into a groove that no longer serves. Drive is your refusal to let settling become stillness. Your push is an act of love—you move people because you believe they're capable of more.
archetype_tunings.The Witness: Sometimes momentum needs a pause to be real. Listen for when someone needs to *be heard* before they can move again. Drive isn't always speed; sometimes it's the witness who says 'I see you, I hear you'—and suddenly the person finds their own momentum again.
archetype_tunings.The Catalyst: You are the ignition. Listen to what's ready to move but hasn't found its spark yet—the intention that needs a next step, the idea that needs a first action. Momentum begins with you naming it. Drive is your superpower: you turn 'I want to' into 'I'm doing.'
